newsitem.title: USA: Superbowl slows Mississippi traffic at New Orleans.
newsitem.headline: Superbowl slows Mississippi traffic at New Orleans.

text.p: The Coast Guard Tuesday announced temporary restrictions on vessels on the Mississippi River at New Orleans on Superbowl weekend in the area where a freighter rammed a crowded riverfront mall last month.

A safety zone the width of the river will be in force from mile 94.0 to mile 96.6 from 1200 CST/1800 GMT Wednesday until 1200 CST January 29. The operators at marine traffic lights on the river will have the authority to order one-way traffic or other restrictions, a Coast Guard spokesman told Reuters.

The Coast Guard said safety measures were needed because of increased vessel traffic, three scheduled Superbowl fireworks shows, a riverboat race and five passenger vessels moored along the waterfront as floating hotels during the event.
In December, the Liberian-flagged M/V Bright Field lost power and rammed the Riverwalk, a crowded riverfront shipping mall, the same stretch of river that is being restricted.
Although no fatalities were reported, more than 100 people were injured and the runaway freighter narrowly missed two cruise ships and a riverboat casino docked in the same area.

The river will be closed to tankers and tank barges for an hour to an hour-and-a-half on Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights during fireworks shows over the river. It will be closed to all deep draft and towing vessels from 1130 CST to 1300 CST Sunday for the riverboat race.
